In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of oxidative stress in cellular senescence and aging.
a hypothesis that mitochondrial production of O2- plays a key role in the aging process and that the level of O2- generation may be the ultimate determinant of life span potential.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rate of generation of mitochondrial O2-, H2O2 and the products of oxy-radicals, such as 4-hydroxynonenal, increases during aging, whereas the level of antioxidant defense does not.
oxidative stress increases with age and this is the cause of aging and senescence.
the level of mitochondrial oxidative stress increases with age in both flies and mammals, but the rate of mitochondrial oxidative stress is a longevity determinant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mitochondrial production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) is an important factor in the aging process.

the rate of O2- production is the most important determinant of life span in animals, and that the rate of H2O2 production is a good indicator of the rate of mitochondrial generation of O 2 - and, hence, of life span potential.
the rate of O2- production in mitochondria increases with age and that this rate is inversely related to life expectancy in flies and to the MLSP in six mammalian species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of O2- production is a better marker for aging than is the level of antioxidant defense.
mitochondria are the main intracellular sources of oxidative stress, which in turn leads to aging and death.
the mitochondrial generation of reactive oxygen species is a major contributor to cellular senescence and the aging process.
